rules.title: Finite-dimensional vector-space convention

origin.tex:
From now on we will study only finite-dimensional vector spaces.
In the rest of this book we shall take `vector space' to mean 
`finite-dimensional vector space'.

rules.application: Carry the author's convention with material after this source passage; do not rewrite local hypotheses or apply it to earlier text. A source convention is not a claim that every object in a fragment is a vector space.

rules.title: Original magic-square and magic-number definition

origin.tex:
A square matrix is 
\definend{magic}\index{matrix!magic square}\index{magic square!definition}
if each row, column, and diagonal adds to the same
number, the matrix's \definend{magic number}.

rules.application: Retain the equal row, column and both diagonal sums. Semimagic deliberately drops the diagonal condition; do not silently restore it there. Keep exact context separate from selected unit bytes; no complete prerequisite or correctness closure is claimed.

origin.tex:
The dots make the matrix on the right where the
rows, columns, 
and diagonals add to $15$.
Now that the people knew how much to sacrifice,

rules.title: Source engraving and four-by-four magic square

origin.tex:
Another magic square appears in the engraving
\textit{Melencolia I} by D\"urer.
% (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melencolia_I)
\begin{center}
  \includegraphics[height=2.20in]{map/pix/Melencolia.jpg} % wikipedia http://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/14/Melencolia_I_%28Durero%29.jpg
\end{center}
One interpretation is that it depicts melancholy, a depressed state.
The figure, genius,
has a wealth of fascinating things to explore including
the compass, the geometrical solid, the scale, and the hourglass.
But the figure is unmoved; all of the things lie unused.
One of the potential delights, in the upper right,
is a $\nbyn{4}$ matrix whose
rows, columns, and diagonals add to~$34$.

rules.application: Retain the original engraving credit and image, the four-by-four size, and common sum thirty-four. Keep exact context separate from selected unit bytes; no complete prerequisite or correctness closure is claimed.

rules.title: Original interpretation of the bottom-row middle entries

origin.tex:
The middle entries on the bottom row give $1514$, the 
date of the engraving.

rules.application: The adjacent entries form the date 1514; they are not two extra matrix rows or a fifth mathematical column. Keep exact context separate from selected unit bytes; no complete prerequisite or correctness closure is claimed.

rules.title: Original zero-magic-number subspace notation

origin.tex:
The set $\magicsquares_{n,0}$ of $\nbyn{n}$~magic squares with magic number~$0$ 
is another subspace and we will verify the formula for its dimension also:
$n^2-2n-1$ when $n\geq 3$.

rules.application: Preserve the n,0 subscript and the stated n at least three qualification of the accompanying dimension formula. Do not apply that formula to Exercise 3 at n=2. Keep exact context separate from selected unit bytes; no complete prerequisite or correctness closure is claimed.

rules.title: Original magic-square subspace observation

origin.tex:
A sum of two same-sized magic squares is magic and a 
scalar multiple of a magic square is magic so the set of 
$\nbyn{n}$ magic squares
$\magicsquares_n$ is a vector space, a subspace of $\matspace_{\nbyn{n}}$.

rules.application: This preceding observation is the source method being adapted to semimagic squares. Do not include the later dimension claim or any supplied exercise answer. Keep exact context separate from selected unit bytes; no complete prerequisite or correctness closure is claimed.

rules.title: Original trace and its restricted null-space interpretation

origin.tex:
Define the 
\definend{trace}\index{trace}\index{matrix!trace} of a matrix to be
the sum down its upper-left to lower-right diagonal
$\trace (M)=m_{1,1}+\cdots+m_{n,n}$.
Consider the restriction of the trace to the magic squares
$\map{\trace}{\magicsquares_n}{\Re}$. 
The null space $\nullspace{\trace}$ is the set of magic squares with magic
number zero 
$\magicsquares_{n,0}$.

rules.application: Retain the diagonal orientation and distinction between trace on all matrices and its restriction to magic squares. The question itself defines the other diagonal. Keep exact context separate from selected unit bytes; no complete prerequisite or correctness closure is claimed.

rules.title: Given question for supplied answer 1

origin.tex:
\item Let $M$ be a $\nbyn{3}$ magic square with magic number~$s$.
    \begin{exparts}
      \partsitem Prove that the sum of $M$'s entries is $3s$.
      \partsitem Prove that $s=3\cdot m_{2,2}$.
      \partsitem Prove that $m_{2,2}$ is the average of the entries
        in its row, its column, and in each diagonal.
      \partsitem Prove that $m_{2,2}$ is the median of $M$'s entries.
    \end{exparts}

rules.application: ANSWER VIEW ONLY. Retain the original hypotheses and every active question part; no other supplied answer or commented-out alternative is a context origin. Keep exact context separate from selected unit bytes; no complete prerequisite or correctness closure is claimed.

rules.title: Given question for supplied answer 4

origin.tex:
\item   \label{exer:TraceIsLinear}
    Let the \definend{trace} function be 
    $\trace (M)=m_{1,1}+\cdots+m_{n,n}$.
    Define also
    the sum down the other diagonal
    $\trace^* (M)=m_{1,n}+\cdots+m_{n,1}$.
    \begin{exparts}
      \partsitem 
        Show that the two functions 
        $\map{\trace,\trace^*}{\matspace_{\nbyn{n}}}{\Re}$
        are linear.
      \partsitem
        Show that the function
       $\map{\theta}{\matspace_{\nbyn{n}}}{\Re^2}$
       given by $\theta(M)=(\trace(M),\trace^*(m))$
       is linear.
     \partsitem
       Generalize the prior item. 
    \end{exparts}

editorial_notes.text: The opening dimension formula says n²−n for magic squares when n≥3. The same active text gives dim M_n=1+dim M_n,0 and dim M_n,0=n²−2n−1, which instead imply n²−2n. Exact rational rank replay gives dimension 3, not 6, at n=3, and agrees with n²−2n for n=3 through 12. The finite replay is not a new proof for all n; the original formula is preserved and this warning is separate.

The proof twice indexes inner columns by 2,…,n−2. The described first-block inner columns are 2,…,n−1: the source itself says column 2 for n=3 and columns 2 and 3 for n=4. The source coefficient arrays confirm those entries. Both occurrences are preserved unchanged.

Exact symbolic replay verifies these discrepancies; a=b=c=d=s/2 does satisfy the original six equations. Original arrows and matrices are unchanged.
